title: Pizza Margherita

ingredients.title: Dough (Neapolitan-Style, 48h Fermentation for Best Flavor)
items: 500 g “00” flour (finely milled Italian pizza flour; substitute bread flour if unavailable)
2 g fresh yeast (or 1 g instant yeast)

ingredients.title: Sauce (San Marzano Tomato Base)
items: 400 g canned San Marzano tomatoes (DOP if possible)
1 small garlic clove, lightly crushed (optional, traditional recipes skip it)

ingredients.title: Toppings
items: 250 g fresh mozzarella di bufala (buffalo mozzarella), drained and torn into chunks
Extra virgin olive oil (high quality, for drizzling)
Fresh basil leaves (8–10 leaves, hand-torn just before baking)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Dough Preparation
steps: Dissolve yeast in water. Gradually mix in flour and salt.
Knead gently until smooth (about 10 minutes by hand or 5 minutes with a mixer).
Cover and let rest for 1 hour at room temperature.
Transfer to the fridge for 24–48 hours cold fermentation (this develops flavor and airy texture).
Remove from fridge 2 hours before baking. Divide into 2 balls and rest at room temp, covered.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Sauce Preparation
steps: Blend San Marzano tomatoes briefly (keep texture, don't over-purée).
Mix with olive oil, pinch of salt, and basil.
Do not cook the sauce—true Neapolitan style uses raw tomato sauce.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Shaping & Assembly
steps: Preheat oven to 250–300°C (480–570°F) with a pizza stone or steel (at least 45 min).
Gently stretch dough ball into a 10–12 inch round, leaving a slightly raised edge (cornicione). Avoid using a rolling pin.
Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce (about 3 tbsp) evenly.
Drizzle lightly with extra virgin olive oil.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Baking
steps: Bake on stone/steel for 6–8 minutes until crust is puffed and charred in spots, cheese melted, and sauce bubbling.
In a wood-fired oven (~430°C / 800°F), it will bake in 60–90 seconds.

chefTips: Use buffalo mozzarella for authenticity, but fior di latte (cow's milk mozzarella) works well.
Always drain mozzarella well to avoid soggy pizza.
A drizzle of high-quality olive oil after baking elevates flavor.
For a restaurant-level touch, serve immediately on a warm pizza plate.
